title_vi: B-tree và LSM-tree: trả giá lúc ghi hay lúc gộp

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a partial clone of the source repository; git hash-object of the retrieved body matches the source-map blob. No source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Ghi nối tiếp và gom lô cũng là lý do Kafka nhanh.
Cơ sở dữ liệu chuỗi thời gian dùng bộ máy lưu trữ kiểu LSM.

claims.evidence: SQLite's btreeInt.h and wal.c (3.45.1), LevelDB's doc/impl.md and RocksDB's options.h, advanced_options.h and filter_policy.h (9.8.4) were read from partial clones of sqlite/sqlite, google/leveldb and facebook/rocksdb at pinned commits; the load times, bytes written and lookup times were measured by the author, who ran one million random keys into SQLite 3.45.1 and RocksDB 9.8.4 (rocksdict 0.3.29) on 2026-10-18.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered lesson.md (markdown-it, tables enabled, every <details> open, a 16 px page gutter) at each width: the page never scrolled sideways and the figure was scaled to the column; the smallest SVG font-size times that scale is the recorded minimum at 320 px. `python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser` measured every line of the figure in Chromium inside its box. Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: Each B-tree page holds N entries and N+1 pointers to subpages; finding a key reads O(log M) pages; a WAL frame is a 24-byte header followed by a full page, and checkpoints copy WAL content back into the database file.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of sqlite/sqlite at tag version-3.45.1 (commit 189e44dfecdc7868bb860dfb5d98eab371318c37).

claims.claim_vi: Updates are appended to a log and kept in a memtable; a full memtable becomes a sorted table in level-0; level-0 files may overlap, files in other levels do not; when a level exceeds its size, a file is merged with the overlapping files of the next level using only bulk reads and writes.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of google/leveldb at commit bb74ef739973a70ca9f0d90788a1da89b788c0ad.

claims.claim_vi: RocksDB 9.8.4 defaults: write_buffer_size 64 MB, max_bytes_for_level_base 256 MB, level0_file_num_compaction_trigger 4, level0_slowdown_writes_trigger 20, level0_stop_writes_trigger 36, level_compaction_dynamic_level_bytes true (from an empty DB the last level is the base level); a Bloom filter of about 10 bits per key gives about 1% false positives.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of facebook/rocksdb at tag v9.8.4 (commit 44e95d8af5d7ec503b3f1d5754c3379ab6c29a9d).

claims.claim_vi: Measured with 1,000,000 random 16-byte keys and 100-byte values (116 MB), no fsync, bytes written counted as the process's wchar: SQLite WITHOUT ROWID in WAL mode committing every 1,000 rows wrote 12,481 MB (107.6x) with a 2 MiB cache and 12,169 MB (104.9x) with 256 MiB; one transaction with 256 MiB wrote 281 MB (2.4x) in 6.3 s; RocksDB with a 4 MiB memtable and 16 MiB level base wrote 621 MB (5.4x) in 3.7 s; 100,000 missing-key lookups took 0.07 s with a 10-bit Bloom filter and 0.74 s without; a 300,000-key run with default RocksDB options produced one level-0 file and no compaction.
claims.verified_by: The author ran and measured this on 2026-10-18 on one machine; hit lookups were dominated by Python overhead and are not compared.

claims.claim_vi: B-tree is the most widely used index structure in relational databases and stores data in pages; LSM-trees are used by Cassandra, LevelDB and RocksDB, persist sorted string tables and compact level 0 into level 1; B-tree enables faster reads, LSM-tree faster writes.

design_notes_vi: Hai thẻ cấu trúc, bốn bước thử với số byte đã ghi đo thật, bốn ghi chú chọn theo việc. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source states that B-tree reads are faster and LSM-tree writes are faster; the lesson measures that B-tree write cost depends on how many pages each commit touches (2.4x in one transaction, over 100x committing every 1,000 rows) and does not claim a read result, because the data was cached.
The source says level 0 is merged into level 1; the lesson notes that RocksDB's default dynamic level sizing makes the last level the base level, as the experiment showed.
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
